newsitem.title: USA: Omnipoint launches digital wireless service in New York.
newsitem.headline: Omnipoint launches digital wireless service in New York.

text.p: Omnipoint Corp. Thursday launched its Personal Communications Services digital mobile phone service in metropolitan New York, with service packages priced between $19.99 and $39.99 per month.
Omnipoint said the new lightweight phones offer greater clarity than analogue cellular services, with few dropped calls, and no risk of the system overload that has plagued cellular service.
The new small phones' capabilities include e-mail, voice mail, faxmail and pager services, as well as longer battery life than existing cellular phones.
The move is the latest challenge to existing providers of cellular service and is expected to attract millions of new customers through low prices and new features, analysts said.
Call rates start at 25 cents per minute for local calls made off peak and on weekends. Calls for anywhere in the United States and Canada are 69 per minute.
Five dollars of usage is included with each service package, with an automatic 5 percent discount for every $50 worth of billed usage, to a 25 percent maximum.
International calls range from 99 cents per minute to $1.99 per minute. Omnipoint uses the Global System for Mobile communications, or GSM, standard, which is common outside the United States.
Omnipoint President George Schmitt said the simplicity of the calling package would bring in extra customers.

Unlike most cellular carriers, Omnipoint will not add long distance or other charges to its air time charges, he said. He also said Omnipoint would not use contracts to retain customers, and those unhappy within 30 days would get a refund.
"There will be no asterisks or fine print in our advertising, not now, not ever," he told a news conference.

Schmitt said he also expected the security offered by the service's encrypted signals to attract lawyers and bankers who steered away from cellular service because of the fear of electronic eavesdropping.
He said users would soon be able to take their phones to almost 100 countries and call home. The bill would arrive, in dollars, when they return.

Battery life for the new phones allows between one and 2-1/2 hours of conversation and 30-72 hours on standby mode -- when calls can be received. That is about twice as long as existing cellular phones.
The phones, which start at $199, are supplied by Telefon AB L.M. Ericsson of Sweden, Nokia Group of Finland, and Motorola Inc. They weigh between seven and eight ounces.

Phones from other manufacturers will follow soon, Schmitt said, noting that a new generation of phones weighing less than seven ounces would be available in a year or so, including a GSM version of Motorola's Startac phone.

Omnipoint's license areas cover 40 million people in the Northeast, though the service launched Thursday covers only metropolitan New York. However, roaming agreements are in place with other U.S. users of GSM systems.

They will soon allow Omnipoint customers to use their phones in parts of Alabama through BellSouth Corp., parts of California through Pacific Telesis Group., and the Washington-Baltimore region of American Personal Communications.
